Kazakh schoolboy wins gold, ranks fifth at global programming Olympiad | Kazakhstan Today

25.08.2026, 19:20 3146

# Kazakh schoolboy wins gold, ranks fifth at global programming Olympiad

Images | gov.kz

Kazakh school student Maksim Tsoi won a gold medal and finished fifth in the individual standings at the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI 2026) in Tashkent, Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Education said.

Three other members of Kazakhstan’s team - Mansur Mamadakhunov, Asqar Azhekan and Aldiyar Seitbay - won silver medals. The national team was prepared for the competition by Temirlan Satylkhanov and Aibek Kuanyshbay.

> "Kazakhstan ranked 10th in the world team standings. This is one of the country’s best results in the history of its participation in the Olympiad," the ministry said.

Earlier, Astana hosted the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence, which brought together more than 500 school students from 106 countries. Participants developed artificial intelligence models and programmed autonomous robots as part of the competition.

New rules for electric scooter users took effect in Kazakhstan on Tuesday. E-scooters are now banned from pavements and pedestrian paths, according to the Almaty Police Department.

Only people aged 18 and over who hold a driving licence of any category and wear a protective helmet are allowed to ride e-scooters on the road. Reflective elements must also be worn when riding after dark.

> "The main change is that electric scooters are prohibited from being ridden on pavements and pedestrian paths. At the same time, riding on the road is permitted only for adults who hold a driving licence of any category and wear a protective helmet," said Abdinur Tasybayev, head of the Administrative Police Department of the Almaty Police Department.

Carrying passengers or cargo on an e-scooter is also prohibited. Riders must dismount when crossing at pedestrian crossings.

Additional requirements apply to rental e-scooters. They must have registration numbers and compulsory insurance. E-scooter rental operators are required to monitor the technical condition, speed and location of their vehicles.

In Almaty, the Sergek traffic monitoring system will be used to detect violations committed by e-scooter riders. Compliance with the rules will also be monitored by patrol officers, district police inspectors and specialised e-scooter patrol units.

Since the beginning of the year, more than 18,000 e-scooter users in Almaty have been held accountable for traffic violations.

New rules for issuing passports to Kazakh citizens living abroad will take effect on September 1, 2026. The relevant order of the Minister of Foreign Affairs was adopted on August 17.

The public service is provided by the Interior Ministry through Kazakhstan’s diplomatic missions and consular offices abroad. Citizens eligible to apply for a passport overseas include those permanently living outside Kazakhstan, studying or working abroad, as well as their family members.

The service is also available to children born outside Kazakhstan, family members of foreigners living abroad, relatives of diplomatic service employees who live with them, elderly people who are unable to care for themselves, people with health-related disabilities, and those caring for such close relatives.

Kazakh citizens who have been detained, held in custody or under arrest, or serving sentences in foreign countries will also be able to apply for passports.

The processing time will depend on whether the diplomatic mission has access to the digital system known as the "Registration Point for Documentation and Population Registration for Foreign Missions". Where access is available, the service must be provided within 40 working days. Without access, the process may take up to 90 calendar days.

Applicants will have to wait no more than 30 minutes for an appointment to submit their documents, while the actual service should take no more than 10 minutes.

If deficiencies are found in the documents, applicants will be given time to correct them. This period will not count towards the overall processing time. Once the documents are corrected, the processing period will resume. If the deficiencies are not corrected within the allotted time, the application will be rejected, with the reason provided.

A separate procedure will apply to children under 14 applying for a passport for the first time who do not have an individual identification number. The diplomatic mission must initiate the process of obtaining the identification number within two working days of receiving the documents. The Interior Ministry will also have two working days to issue the identification number or reject the application.

The completed passport must be collected in person by the applicant or their legal representative.

The new rules will take effect on September 1, 2026.

Kazakh school student among world’s top five young programmers - JIJI PRESS

# Kazakh school student among world’s top five young programmers

Kazakh school student among world’s top five young programmers

 The International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) 2026 has concluded in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, with 375 students from 92 countries competing, Qazinform News Agency cites Kazakhstan's Ministry of Enlightenment. All four members of the Kazakhstan team won medals – one gold and three silver. In the overall team standings, Kazakhstan placed 10th, one of the country's best results in its history at the Olympiad. Maxim Tsoi, a 12th-grade student at Spectrum International School in Astana, won gold and finished 5th in the individual world rankings. The silver medalists are: 

- Aldiyar Seitbay – 11th-grade student at the Astana Bilim-Innovation Boarding Lyceum for Boys
- Mansur Mamadakhunov – 11th-grade student at the Kyzylorda Region Bilim-Innovation Boarding Lyceum for Boys
- Askar Akezhan – 12th-grade student at the Nazarbayev Intellectual School of Science and Mathematics in Semey

 Kazakhstan's team coaches: Temirlan Satylkhanov – head coach from Astana IT University Aibar Kuanyshbay – senior lecturer, International Information Technologies University In 2025, Kazakh students won three silver and one bronze medal, ranking 14th. This year, the team improved its standing by four positions. Kazakh school students have claimed 79 medals at the International Olympiad in Informatics over the years. Earlier, Qaziform reported that a Kazakh school student ranked among the top 3 at the International Olympiad in AI.
